usageNotes: Use this to poll the live runtime state of a specific QEMU VM — power state, CPU/memory usage, uptime, and I/O counters since last boot. The caller must have VM.Audit permission on /vms/{vmid} and the target node must be reachable in the cluster; querying a VM on an offline node returns an error, not a stopped status. Check the 'lock' field before issuing any write operations (migrate, backup, snapshot) — a non-empty lock means another task already owns the VM.

examples.summary: Get current status of VM 101 on node pve1

tips: The 'status' field returns only 'stopped' or 'running'; use 'qmpstatus' for finer-grained QEMU states such as 'paused' or 'prelaunch'.
diskread/diskwrite counters reset to zero on each VM start; they are cumulative since last boot, not lifetime totals.
mem reflects ballooning-reported usage when the guest agent supports it; memhost reflects actual host-level allocation — these can differ significantly under memory pressure.
The 'ha' object is always present but will be empty/minimal if HA is not configured for the VM.
Pressure stall metrics (pressurecpu*, pressureio*, pressuremem*) require a Linux host kernel with PSI support and are absent on older PVE hosts.
